units.name: Yellowstone River
units.writeup: The Yellowstone River Unit covers southwestern and south-central Montana and extends south to include Yellowstone National Park. This unit has a diverse operational footprint that includes several wildland fire engines, four helitack crews, an interagency dispatch center, a wildland fire module, Type 2 IA Veteran crew, a large airtanker base and one direct service tribal program. The unit is strongly suppression and aviation oriented, while also carrying a substantial fuels management workload.

units.name: Triple Divide
units.writeup: The Triple Divide Unit encompasses northwestern Montana, including Glacier National Park and adjoining areas east and west of the Continental Divide. This unit includes both a fuels management and fire suppression organization, along with two 638 contract/compact tribal programs. The unit's workload combines wildfire suppression with significant protection and partnership responsibilities, particularly across tribal, federal, and interagency jurisdictions.

units.name: Northern Plains
units.writeup: The Northern Plains Unit encompasses North Dakota and represents the easternmost portion of the Northern Rockies Geographic Area. The unit has several engines, one direct service tribal program and two 638 contract/compact tribal programs. The workload is predominantly initial attack and fuels management/prescribed fire, split roughly evenly between grassland and prairie fire environments and juniper, ponderosa pine, and hardwood fuel models, with extensive tribal, federal, state, and local coordination across a geographically dispersed area.

units.name: Bitterroot Range
units.writeup: The Bitterroot Range Unit covers north Idaho and western Montana, extending from the Idaho Panhandle south through the Bitterroot landscape. The unit is primarily a fuels management organization that includes two 638 contract tribal programs, with significant interagency and tribal coordination responsibilities. Its workload reflects a mix of direct suppression and substantial protection responsibilities, including complex federal, tribal, and interagency landscapes.

units.name: Tongue River
units.writeup: The Tongue River Unit covers southeastern and much of eastern Montana, with an additional area extending into northwestern South Dakota. This unit has a substantial ground-based suppression organization, including several wildland fire engines, a suppression module, an interagency dispatch center, a single engine airtanker base, and one direct service tribal program providing a substantial initial-attack and aviation capability across a large geographic footprint. The workload is heavily influenced by fast-moving grassland fire and suppression response, balanced with fuels management responsibilities across intermingled federal, tribal, state, and local jurisdictions.

units.name: Missouri Breaks
units.writeup: The Missouri Breaks Unit spans north-central Montana, including the Missouri River and breaks country extending toward the Canadian border. This unit has a substantial ground-based suppression organization, including several wildland fire engines, a wildland fire module, an interagency dispatch center, two direct service tribal programs and one 638 compact tribal program. Its workload reflects a strong combination of initial attack/suppression capacity and broad fuels management responsibilities across dispersed federal, tribal, and interagency lands.
